title: Imperfect Middle and Passive
description: The imperfect middle and passive, the neuter plural subject with a singular verb, and the uses of καί and οὐδέ.

blocks.caption: Summary
blocks.html: As in the present, the middle and passive of the imperfect have the same forms. They are made like the imperfect active, with the augment and the secondary middle endings -μην, -σο, -το, -μεθα, -σθε, -ντο.

blocks.caption: ἐλυόμην, I was being loosed
rows: ἐλύου comes from ἐλύεσο with the σ dropped. A verb deponent in the present is deponent in the imperfect too: ἠρχόμην, I was coming.

blocks.caption: Neuter plural subject
blocks.html: A neuter plural subject may take a singular verb: τὰ δαιμόνια ἐξέρχεται, the demons go out. The New Testament often uses the plural verb as well; the course accepts both.

blocks.caption: καί and οὐδέ
blocks.html: καί means and, also or even; καί … καί means both … and. οὐδέ means and not, nor, not even; οὐδέ … οὐδέ means neither … nor.
